label: Late in episodes, D1 drops after no reward and rises after reward; GO tracks S2-belief.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (in_rew == 1) * np.square(ep_trial) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * np.square(ep_trial)
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward==0)*(prev_state==1) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_reward == 1) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 1) * ep_trial**2 ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2)==1) * ep_trial**2
explanation: Raw candidate n36 sits saturated near +1 early in episodes and desaturates late (timing baseline). Beyond timing, every effect grows roughly with ep_trial squared (constant-size terms reach only ~0.24 dev, ep_trial-linear 0.30, ep_trial^2 0.59): at D1 the previous reward input pushes it up when rewarded and down when unrewarded, and at GO it is higher when the ideal observer believes S2 is good (negative weight on belief_lo). D2 is ~1 throughout. The free fit adds that an unrewarded S2 visit lowers D1 more than an unrewarded S1 visit (a1 S2 u strongest), a small D1 belief term, GO terms for the last reward and choice, and the reward two trials back; the short form misses the S2-vs-S1 asymmetry (over-predicts D1 after a1 S2 u, under-predicts after S1 u). Observed-only; no future variables.

issues: The label says D1 'drops after no reward', but the profile residuals show the drop comes almost entirely from unrewarded S2 visits: a1 S2 u -0.246 and a2 S2 u -0.152, against a1 S1 u -0.026 and a2 S1 u -0.008. A reader would expect a fall after any unrewarded trial, which is wrong for S1.

Misses on the recorded short form show this as the largest systematic error. D1 after a1 S2 u is over-predicted by -0.147, and D1 after a2 S1 u and a1 S1 u are under-predicted by +0.091 and +0.071. The explanation admits this, but the label does not.

The short form cannot express the S2-only drop because of the factor limit. (phase==D1)*((prev_state==2)&(prev_reward==0))*ep^2 is rejected as 4 factors. The legal alternatives score lower on test: the additive prev_state==2 term 0.417, last_is('a1 S2 u') 0.468, and (in_rew - (prev_state==2)) 0.485, all against 0.526 for the recorded form.

The other claims hold up on test. Taking out the GO belief term drops R^2 from 0.526 to 0.396. ep_trial^2 beats ep_trial (0.501), and exp(ep_trial/20) gives about the same (0.524). belief_lo beats raw belief at GO (0.454) and beats prev_action (0.460). Applying belief to both D1 and GO does not help (0.519). The recorded form is close to the 0.53 additive ceiling and reaches 85% of the free fit.

Minor: the (in_rew==1) term has no phase factor, but it is in effect a D1-only term, so its label reading is fine. Some worst-fit windows are late-episode runs of persistent a1 choices where GO is far below the prediction (actual ~0.01 vs predicted ~0.5). The GO belief term only partly captures these.
The label leaves out D2, where the value stays saturated at about 1 with no effect.
